heading: Sample callback
text:
### Sample callback [NSTG.5.3]

Fires **once per absorbed sample**, during fact assertion and after the
firing decision has landed ([LSER.8.6]) — so a sample is delivered only
when the assertion that produced it survived, never speculatively.

Each sample identifies itself fully, so a receiver needs no prior state:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| schema_name / slot_name | which declared series this belongs to |
| identity_slot_name / identity_value | which series instance — **both empty under `by: none`**, where the series is not partitioned |
| ts_ns | the engine clock at absorption |
| value | the sampled value, typed to match the slot |

Two things follow. The empty-identity convention means a receiver must
treat empty as *unpartitioned* rather than as a missing field. And
because the timestamp is the **absorption** instant from the engine
clock, samples stay correctly ordered and replay-reproducible however the
integrator batches the writes.

The callback signature will be `ds_sample_cb_t` and the sample struct
`ds_sample_t`, declared in `runtime/include/libds.h` when this section binds.
Nothing declares them in this edition.
